Streets, schools and getting around Quilchena

items.t: Quilchena is a pocket in the City of Richmond, BC, in west Richmond around Quilchena Elementary School at 3760 Moresby Drive, near Granville Avenue and Railway Avenue. No official boundary is published for a Quilchena neighbourhood, and Quilchena is not listed as a City of Richmond OCP area or sub-area plan name; the City plan context for the Granville Avenue / Railway Avenue bend is the Laurelwood Sub-Area Plan. Nearby: the Laurelwood / Granville Avenue bend to the north, Terra Nova to the north-west, Seafair to the south-west, and Richmond City Centre to the east.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not. The documented housing form for this pocket is detached houses under the Single Detached RS1/RS2 zones, and no named condo building or townhome complex in the pocket was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source. The nearest transit anchor is outside the pocket: Richmond-Brighouse Station (Canada Line) on No. 3 Road, east of the pocket, identified by the City as a Transit-Oriented Area.

Local anchors: Quilchena Elementary School, 3760 Moresby Drive; Thompson Community Centre, 5151 Granville Avenue, north across Granville Avenue; Richmond Public Library Brighouse (Main) Branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate, in the City Centre; Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway.

Transit: TransLink route 401 (One Road) — Richmond-Brighouse Station via No. 3 Road, Westminster Highway and No. 1 Road to Steveston — is the route confirmed on an official timetable for the wider west Richmond road network.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Quilchena

items.t: Suites / SSMUH: the City states at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit such as a coach house is allowed per lot on covered lots, with Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (RSM) zoning applied under Bill 44 and provincial minimums of three units on lots 280 m² or less and four units on larger lots — the realistic "multi-unit" route in this pocket is a house lot, not a condo building.

The name is a school, not a plan. "Quilchena" in Richmond names a pocket after its elementary school; the City has no Quilchena OCP area, sub-area plan or published boundary. The plan document that actually describes this bend of Granville Avenue and Railway Avenue is the Laurelwood Sub-Area Plan.

The 55+ building with the same name is in a different neighbourhood. Quilchena Green (91 units, known 55+) sits in Terra Nova. Buyers, and some listing copy, merge the two because of the shared name — the strata documents for any "Quilchena" unit will show a Terra Nova address if it is that building.

The whole city is designated flood plain — by bylaw, not by map shading. Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204 designates all lands in Richmond as flood plain and sets the flood construction levels habitable floors must meet; the dike system behind that designation is designed for a 1:500 event and is being raised from 3.5 m to 4.7 m for sea level rise.

SD38 has no middle schools. A family moving from a three-tier district (for example Mission's SD75) will find Richmond runs elementary K–7 and secondary 8–12 only — the "middle school" question has no answer here, and the feeder pattern (Quilchena Elementary into Hugh Boyd Secondary) is published on the secondary school's own site.

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: in completed form, nowhere inside the pocket. The documented housing form for this pocket is detached houses under the Single Detached RS1/RS2 zones. The pocket's one townhouse project, Quilchena West at 3888 Moresby Drive, is a presale. The nearest transit anchor is outside the pocket: Richmond-Brighouse Station (Canada Line) on No. 3 Road, east of the pocket, identified by the City as a Transit-Oriented Area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Quilchena

items.t: Form B diligence (strata purchases generally, and Quilchena West resales later): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. A presale purchase itself runs on the developer's disclosure statement instead (REDMA, below).
Fee-simple homes (the pocket's actual stock): A secondary suite is a permitted secondary use in the RS1/RS2 zones.

Richmond zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw 8500 governs — Single Detached (RS1/RS2), Section 8.1, is the common single-family zoning in this pocket, with minimum lot areas by subzone including 360 m² (RS1/B, RS2/B), 550 m² (RS1/E), 828 m² (RS1/F) and 2,000 m² (RS1/G), and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. The city-wide plan is Richmond's 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000, with area and sub-area plans held in Schedule 2 under Bylaws 7100 and 9000; the Laurelwood Sub-Area Plan is the City sub-area plan for the Granville Avenue / Railway Avenue bend.

Presales (REDMA) — Quilchena West: a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust.

blocks.text: Good to know about Quilchena townhomes

items.t: The pocket's first townhouse complex is being sold from a mall in another neighbourhood. Quilchena West's sales gallery sits at 188-8120 No. 2 Road (Blundell Centre), not on the Moresby Drive site — a buyer who drives to Moresby Drive looking for a show home will find a construction site and a school, which is the correct mental picture of this pocket today.
The 55+ building with the same name is in a different neighbourhood — and its age label disagrees with itself.

The pocket's lot sizes swing by a factor of five by subzone. RS1/RS2 subdivision minimums in Zoning Bylaw 8500 run from 360 m² (RS1/B, RS2/B) through 550 m² (RS1/E) and 828 m² (RS1/F) to 2,000 m² (RS1/G) — two "Quilchena houses" a few streets apart can sit in different subzones with different suite, coach-house and SSMUH math. Confirm the subzone before pricing any added-unit value.

Established-street house lots: predominantly freehold detached houses on the pocket's residential streets under Single Detached (RS1 / RS2) in Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500, Section 8.1, with a secondary suite listed as a permitted secondary use.

Lot character from the zone ladder, as stated: RS1 / RS2 subzone subdivision minimums in Section 8.1 include 360 m² for RS1/B and RS2/B, 550 m² for RS1/E, 828 m² for RS1/F and 2,000 m² for RS1/G. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the subzone for a specific lot is confirmed with the City.
Do not assume a servicing position for a specific lot; confirm water, sewer and drainage connections with the City parcel by parcel.

Flood position — applies to every lot: Richmond is made up of islands within the floodplain of the Fraser River at an average of 1 metre above sea level, protected by 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way; all lands in Richmond are designated flood plain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204, which sets flood construction levels (FCLs) habitable floors must meet unless an exemption applies.
Land has no SnapStats category in any case.

Quilchena West — 3888 Moresby Drive. A strata TOWNHOME presale inside the pocket — housing, not lots: It is cross-referenced here once as the pocket's one current development site and is not re-documented as land stock: a buyer there buys a strata townhome, not a lot, and there is no lot offering within it.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Quilchena

items.t: Flood — the defining lot rule in Richmond: all lands are designated flood plain under Bylaw No. 8204 and habitable floors must meet the FCL for the area unless exempt; confirm the lot's FCL, and any flood covenant on title, before planning a build or major renovation.

Richmond property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid 2026 taxes after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% penalty on any outstanding balance after September 1, 2026. Annual flat-rate utility payments were due March 31, 2026, with a 10% discount only for payments received on or before the due date; the City's discounted cost for a typical single-family metered residence for 2026 totals $2,251 per year (water $631, sewer $835, garbage/recycling/environmental programs $443, flood protection $342) — the $342 flood-protection line is a holding cost on every Richmond lot.

blocks.text: Good to know about Quilchena lots

items.t: There is no official Quilchena to draw on a map: the City publishes no boundary and no OCP plan name for Quilchena — the plan context is the Laurelwood Sub-Area Plan for the Granville / Railway bend. Describe a lot by its anchors (Quilchena Elementary, Moresby Drive, Granville Avenue, Railway Avenue), not by lines the City has not published.

The pocket's one development site sells homes, not land: Quilchena West at 3888 Moresby Drive is a 110-townhome presale (project brochure) on a Moresby Drive site inside the pocket — its arrival changes the pocket's housing mix without creating any buyable lot.

Richmond's flood-protection charge is inside the ordinary utility bill: $342 of the typical single-family metered utility total of $2,251 for 2026 is flood protection — the dike system is a line item every lot owner pays, not an abstraction.
